problem_type: Agent-visible capability has no executable owner
symptom: The Agent can be shown tools such as storyboard/timeline/staging/camera actions and author_skill, but invoking them can return no execution or leave the project and Skill library unchanged.
direct_cause: Tool descriptors and policy projections were extended without registering every alias in the canonical capability registry and without routing every registered alias through a Host-owned transport adapter to its domain owner. Skill listing and reading also use different visibility predicates across Pi, MCP, and Agent surfaces.
class_root: Nomi has no enforced invariant that every model-visible tool name resolves to exactly one canonical capability, one transport adapter, and one domain-owner effect, with the same visibility decision across all Skill consumers.
affected_population: Users asking the Agent to create storyboards, arrange a timeline, create staging references, or set camera moves
Users asking the Agent to author or apply a Skill
Users whose repository or installed Skills are visible in one Agent surface but absent or unreadable in another
Future tools added to a descriptor or policy list without a corresponding registry and owner route
entry_points: Canvas write transport and Host execution coordinator
internal_only_reason: The invariant is an internal Nomi capability registry, transport, Host ownership, and Skill visibility contract; no provider or third-party API decides whether a visible tool has a local domain owner.
invariants: Every model-visible tool name maps to one canonical registry capability and one executable transport adapter; an unmapped descriptor cannot be advertised.
Every write-capable alias is admitted by the Host and performs its effect through the owning domain service; unknown aliases fail closed with a structured error and never return a false success.
Canvas storyboard, timeline, staging, and camera aliases preserve the existing domain owner and transaction/undo semantics rather than creating a second state store.
author_skill uses the Skill library owner and cannot mutate only a chat transcript or silently disappear.
Pi, Agent, and MCP Skill list/read/resource projections consume one origin-aware visibility/catalog decision and the same package version/content hash.
A capability or Skill manifest can only shrink the Host ceiling; it cannot register a new tool or widen authority.
generality_proof: Descriptor, policy, registry, transport, and Host execution are shared boundaries for every current and future Agent tool. The registry-to-adapter coverage test enumerates all advertised aliases, while the visibility contract is consumed by Pi, Agent, and MCP projections. Therefore a new alias cannot become visible without either an executable owner route or a failing focused test, and an invocation cannot silently report success when no domain effect occurred.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Own the canonical capability IDs, aliases, schemas, and domain ownership used by every projection.
Resolve admitted Canvas aliases to the real canvas/timeline/staging owner and fail closed for unknown aliases.
Make the ProjectAgentHost the sole admission and execution path for write effects, preserving one history and queue.
Apply one origin-aware Skill visibility decision and immutable package identity to all list/read consumers.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: These aliases are model-visible and now must be covered by the canonical registry and Canvas transport adapter coverage test.
The alias is model-visible in creation/Agent policy and is routed through the Skill library owner rather than remaining an old Creation-only handler.
Pi and MCP/Agent consumers are checked against the shared visibility and package identity contract.
MCP metadata/content and write dispatch are required to use the same canonical registry/visibility boundaries.

recurrence.reason: Any future descriptor, policy, Skill, or transport alias can repeat the same visible-but-unexecutable failure unless coverage is enforced at the shared registry and adapter boundaries.
same_class_scan: Enumerated all Agent tool descriptors and compared their names with the canonical capability registry and transport adapter switch.
Searched Host execution coordinator and every document/canvas/timeline write adapter for aliases that can return null or bypass the Host owner.
Compared Pi Skill roots, Agent load_skill, Skill store list/read, MCP skills.list/read, resources/list/read, and prompts/list/get for divergent origin/audience filters and identity fields.

prevention.invariant: An advertised write tool must have a canonical registry entry, an executable adapter, and a domain-owner effect; Skill visibility/read must use one origin-aware catalog decision.
prevention.failure_mode: Missing registry/adapter coverage fails the focused contract test; an unknown runtime alias returns a structured capability error and performs no write; a mismatched Skill identity is rejected and requires relisting.
prevention.strategy: Make the registry and visibility catalog the earliest shared boundaries, derive all descriptors from them, and keep domain writes behind the Host-owned adapters. Remove old direct/fallback paths in the same change.

retained_compatibility_paths: src/workbench/creation/creationToolCalls.ts (compatibility/test-only; excluded from the production Host graph)
legacy_paths.rationale: Silent unknown-alias fallbacks cannot remain after Host admission is authoritative. The legacy Creation helper remains only for compatibility/tests until its consumers are retired; it is not a second production owner.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No third-party dependency controls the capability or Skill ownership invariant.

migration: Existing Skill packages retain their content and origin metadata; callers with stale MCP resource identities must relist. Existing tool calls continue through their canonical aliases, while removed direct/fallback paths fail visibly rather than being silently replayed.
residual_risks: The final packaged Electron GUI journey still needs to exercise every newly wired alias and verify persisted domain effects; unit/contract coverage alone is not visual acceptance.
Third-party MCP clients may cache older Skill URIs and must handle the documented relist error.
